content:
The test image shows a soybean stem split lengthwise. Key features:
- Bleached white/gray exterior of the stem
- Internal pith appears degraded/rotted with brown discoloration
- The stem tissue looks shredded/fibrous inside
- Stem held in hand, field background

This looks like an internal stem rot. Top candidates: **White_Mold** (bleached exterior, internal rot), **Charcoal_Rot** (gray pith with sclerotia), **Sudden_death_syndrome** (brown pith), **Brown_Stem_Rot**.

Now viewing one reference from each top candidate:

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Split soybean stem held in hand. Exterior is bleached white/gray. Interior shows shredded, fibrous, degraded pith tissue with brown discoloration alongside white tissue. This is a stem cross-section diagnostic view.

- **White_Mold ref (133)**: Shows bleached tan/white stem with black sclerotia on surface — bleached exterior matches the test image well. White Mold (Sclerotinia) causes shredding of the pith and stem bleaching.

- **Charcoal_Rot ref**: Shows field-level yellowing/wilting — no close-up stem split. Charcoal rot would show gray/charcoal pith with tiny black sclerotia.

- **Sudden_death_syndrome ref**: Shows leaf interveinal chlorosis/necrosis — a leaf disease presentation, not matching the stem split in the test image.

The bleached white/tan stem exterior combined with the shredded, fibrous degraded pith interior is highly characteristic of **White Mold** (Sclerotinia stem rot). This disease hollows out and shreds the pith, leaving a bleached stem — exactly what's shown in the split stem view.
